title: Lab awareness, human interaction, and camera cycling

execution_posture.operator_interaction_policy: Do not ask the operator for next steps unless MIM/TOD go off course, safety is uncertain, or credentials/physical access are missing.
execution_posture.next_objective_policy: Drop follow-on objectives directly into MIM for execution. TOD/Codex may create learning objectives only from observed off-course moments.

goal: MIM becomes aware of activity, humans, and objects in its private lab/space, initiates voice interaction with humans, remembers interactions and names, recognizes Dave as primary operator, asks about unknown objects, and cycles all cameras including the arm camera.
success_criteria: When Dave or any human enters the lab, MIM detects the presence and initiates interaction via voice TTS without waiting for typed input.
MIM records each human interaction with timestamp, modality, confidence, summary, and follow-up commitments for future reference.
MIM remembers humans by name when they identify themselves or when a verified recognition binding exists.
MIM knows Dave is the primary operator and treats Dave as the default trusted operator identity unless evidence shows a different identified human.
MIM identifies visible objects in the lab, stores known-object memory, and asks the operator about unknown objects instead of fabricating labels.
MIM cycles all available cameras, including the arm camera, and publishes per-camera reachability/openability/freshness evidence.
MIM distinguishes permission/authority from live sensor truth: it may say the lab resources are authorized, but only claims live seeing/hearing after current capture/openability evidence.
TOD/Codex only intervene when MIM/TOD go off course; each intervention creates or updates a learning objective that prevents recurrence.
constraints: No unsafe hardware movement. Arm camera cycling may use existing safe scan/capture routines only.
No fake recognition. Unknown humans or objects remain unknown until identified with evidence.
No always-on private data leakage. Store summaries and identity bindings needed for continuity, not unnecessary raw transcripts/video.
Respect resource budgets: cycle cameras at bounded intervals and back off when devices are busy or unavailable.
If a camera/microphone is unavailable, publish a setup/repair task instead of treating it as a permission failure.

execution_phases.objective: Inventory all cameras/microphones, including browser, local runtime, and arm camera surfaces.
Cycle cameras and publish latest frame/observation freshness without unsafe movement.
Detect human presence and initiate TTS greeting/interaction.
Store and recall human names and interactions, with Dave as primary operator.
Identify known objects, ask about unknown objects, and store answers.
Continue with direct MIM objectives until success; create learning objectives from off-course events only.

first_task.title: Inventory lab sensors and publish first live-readiness map
acceptance_criteria: Publish MIM_LAB_SENSOR_INVENTORY.latest.json with all detected cameras/microphones and arm camera status.
Publish MIM_LAB_AWARENESS_STATUS.latest.json with current phase, blockers, next MIM-owned action, and evidence links.
Do not claim a human/object/camera is live unless current evidence exists.
If MIM runtime API is down, record service-down as the first off-course event and create a learning/repair objective.

off_course_signals: camera/mic permission confused with live readiness
stale artifact presented as current truth
TOD/Codex tries to take primary execution without evidence
off_course_learning_policy.required_response: Create a bounded learning objective directly in MIM that names the off-course signal, evidence, fix hypothesis, validation, and recurrence guard.
off_course_learning_policy.operator_contact: Only contact Dave when safety, identity, credential, or physical access cannot be resolved autonomously.
